parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file only declares abstract port interfaces: ProductRepository, OrderRepository, Clock and IdGenerator. Their signatures use only domain types (Product, Order, OrderState) and built-ins (Date, string). It contains no persistence implementation, transport, framework code or I/O. In DDD and hexagonal architecture, repository interfaces and similar abstractions belong in the domain layer. The infrastructure layer supplies the concrete classes (InMemory*Repository, SystemClock, UuidGenerator), and the application layer injects them. All of this matches the domain layer's role. Clock and IdGenerator are general-purpose ports, and the file name "repositories.ts" does not describe them. That is a naming and organisation detail, not a responsibility in the wrong layer.
